title: QMA hardness using only unit-charge nuclei in the continuum
exact_target: Is the full antisymmetric continuum electronic Coulomb ground-energy promise problem QMA-hard when every nucleus has charge one, distinct positions are rational, electron count is unary, and rational thresholds are separated by at least inverse input length? Require deterministic polynomial-time reductions producing polynomially many nuclei and electrons, polynomial bit lengths, and gap at least one.
